title: Equipment Safety Inspection Checklist
subtitle: A field-level checklist for inspecting machinery and equipment safety
intro: Machinery and equipment are a leading source of serious workplace injury when guarding, isolation, or maintenance controls fail. This checklist gives inspectors a practical sequence for verifying equipment safety on site, from guarding and lockout through operator competency and emergency stops.

sections.title: Machine Guarding
items: Are all moving parts (belts, chains, gears, blades) fitted with fixed or interlocked guards?
Are guards free of damage, gaps, or unauthorised modification?
Do interlocked guards stop the machine immediately when opened?
Are guards reinstated correctly after maintenance before equipment is returned to service?
Are point-of-operation hazards guarded to prevent hand or body access during operation?

sections.title: Lockout / Tagout
items: Is a documented lockout/tagout procedure available for each piece of equipment?
Are isolation points clearly identified and labelled on the equipment?
Are personal locks and tags used and not shared between workers?
Is a zero-energy state verified before maintenance work begins?
Are lockout/tagout procedures followed for all energy sources, not just electrical?

sections.title: Electrical Safety on Equipment
items: Are electrical enclosures and panels closed, labelled, and free of exposed conductors?
Are cables and connectors free of damage, fraying, or improvised repairs?
Is earthing or bonding intact and verified on relevant equipment?
Are residual current devices or equivalent protection fitted where required?
Are electrical inspections and test tags current and visible?

sections.title: Lifting Equipment & Slings
items: Is lifting equipment (cranes, hoists, forklifts) within its current inspection or load test date?
Are slings, chains, and shackles free of visible wear, deformation, or corrosion?
Is safe working load clearly marked and not exceeded during operation?
Are lifting operations planned and supervised for non-routine or complex lifts?

sections.title: Pressure Equipment
items: Is pressure equipment (compressors, boilers, vessels) within its current statutory inspection date?
Are pressure relief valves fitted, unobstructed, and tested?
Are gauges functional and readings within normal operating range?
Are pressure equipment records and certificates available on site?

sections.title: Maintenance & Service Records
items: Is a documented preventive maintenance schedule followed for each machine?
Are maintenance records up to date and available for inspection?
Are defects identified during maintenance logged and closed out before return to service?
Is equipment taken out of service and tagged when a fault is identified?
Are third-party statutory inspection certificates current for regulated equipment?

sections.title: Operator Competency
items: Are operators trained and certified for the specific equipment they use?
Are competency records current and available for each authorised operator?
Is equipment restricted to authorised operators only, with unauthorised use prevented?
Are refresher training and competency reassessments conducted at a defined interval?

sections.title: Emergency Stops & Safety Devices
items: Are emergency stop controls clearly visible, accessible, and correctly labelled?
Do emergency stops function correctly when tested?
Are light curtains, pressure mats, or other safety devices functioning and unobstructed?
Are alarms and warning indicators (audible or visual) operational on moving equipment?

sections.title: Housekeeping Around Equipment
items: Is the area around equipment kept clear of clutter, spills, and trip hazards?
Are walkways and access routes to equipment unobstructed?
Is equipment kept free of excessive dust, oil, or material build-up that could create a hazard?
Are tools and loose parts stored away from moving machinery when not in use?
